alignments.note: Construct noun with the *the* supplied for it under rule 29, no article morpheme standing in the chain. Headed on *praises* by rule 31's class-noun test: the ASV writes a bare *praise* for a noun of this class elsewhere in the psalm, so *high* is its specifier; the competing reading heads on *high*.
Nomen rectum takes the relational *of* under rule 19.

Verbless clause with a prepositional predicate: the construction-supplied copula joins the preposition heading that phrase under rule 49, and the volitive frame *Let ... be* is the copula the ASV has written in that slot. Discontinuous under rule 25; the ASV's italics corroborate the supply and decide nothing, by rule 7.
The noun takes the word the printed text writes for it; the margin's literal 'Hebrew throat' was read and set aside, by rule 38.
Suffix rendered by the possessive, rule 18.
Conjunction takes the *And* written for it, rule 14.
The indefinite article belongs to the noun that licenses it under rule 15; discontinuous around the attributive under rule 25.
The ASV renders the construct relation attributively rather than with *of*, so the rectum takes *two edged* under rule 28, headed on the word carrying the lexeme.
Preposition; the second colon gaps the copula and the ASV writes none for it, so there is nothing further to place.
Suffix rendered by the possessive, rule 18.

review_notes: The clause is verbless and its predicate is the prepositional phrase, so the whole supplied *Let ... be* frame joins the preposition under rule 49 rather than being marked `added`; the alternative of putting it on the fronted construct nominal was rejected because that nominal is the clause's subject.
`רוֹמְמוֹת` heads on *praises* rather than *high*; both readings are defensible under rule 31 and the class-noun test decided it.
